rules.question: Will {A} take a new pressure measure against {B} in {month}?
counts: A trade measure: Global Trade Alert records a measure by {A}'s government (for the EU, one adopted at EU level) that it rates harmful, aimed explicitly at {B} (named among at most ten countries; GTA's 'targeted', not 'inferred'), of a kind a government can aim at another country: tariffs and other import charges; import or export bans, quotas and licensing; export controls; sanitary, technical and customs rules; financial, investment and payment restrictions; port and channel restrictions. Dated by its announcement (or, without one, its start).

Sanctions: {A}'s government adds at least one person, company or vessel connected to {B} to a sanctions or export-control list, under a programme aimed at {B} itself or a thematic one (human rights, corruption, military end users). Listings under a programme aimed at a third country (a firm in {B} listed for helping another country's government) do not count, nor do counter-terrorism, narcotics, organised crime and cyber-crime listings. Dated by listing.
A WTO dispute: {A} formally opens a dispute with {B} at the World Trade Organization (a request for consultations). Dated by the request.
not_counted: Trade remedies (anti-dumping, anti-subsidy and safeguard duties), subsidies and measures applying to all countries alike.
Renewals or extensions without change (they are not new records in these sources).
rules.resolution: Resolved automatically 90 days after the month ends, from what Global Trade Alert, the sanctions lists and the WTO record by then: yes if any measure above is dated in the month, otherwise no. A measure recorded later does not change a sealed answer. Global Trade Alert often records measures months after they are announced; the back-test uses the same 90-day rule.
rules.pairs: Every direction between the 40 largest economies, Lithuania, Georgia and the EU, leaving out pairs inside the EU (members with each other, and the EU with a member).
rules.warning: An early warning means pressure is rising for the pair: this month's chance is at least twice its usual chance (the model's average for the pair over the previous 12 months) and at least 10%. Pairs that are always under pressure stay near their usual chance and are not flagged, however high it is.

features.name: own_count_36m
features.label: Months with a measure by A against B in the last 36 months (log)

features.name: own_12m
features.label: Any measure by A against B in the last 12 months

features.name: news_tension
features.label: Rise in the share of conflict in the news between A and B (GDELT): the last 3 months against the 2 years before

versions.decision: first version: features chosen by forward selection

explanation: The Brier score is the average squared gap between the forecast and what happened (1 if a measure came, 0 if not): lower is better, and a forecast that always said 0% would score the share of months with a measure.

Each month the model is compared with two simple rules: the base rate (the same chance for every pair, the share of all past pair-months with a measure) and persistence (last month repeats: a higher chance where a measure came last month).

Retrospective back-test, 2016-01 to 2026-06: training uses earlier resolved months. The model's Brier score was 0.00749, against 0.00970 for the base rate and 0.00896 for persistence; it did better than the base rate and persistence. This uses today's versions of the historical data and assumed release lags, not snapshots of what was available then. The features were chosen on the last 60 resolved months of this same period, so it can overstate accuracy; the sealed live record is the independent test.
Live record: the first monthly forecasts are resolved 90 days after their month ends; they will appear here then.
Calibration: of all the times the model said about 10%, a measure should have come about one time in ten.
